q: Which pair consists only of elevator safety devices?
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The governor senses overspeed and the safety gear grips the rails. Comb plates and step chains belong to escalators, and sheaves drive and guide the ropes.

q: A department store wants continuous flow between floors and wants shoppers to see merchandise along the way. Which system fits best?
o: A moving walk on each floor
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Escalators move people without waiting and give an open view of each floor. Stores often arrange them so riders walk past displays between flights.

q: What is the architect's role in elevator and escalator design?
o: Size the drive motors and hoist ropes personally
Leave all shaft sizes for the contractor to fix on site
Coordinate space, access, structure, MEP and fire safety with engineers and makers
Choose the equipment brand before planning the core
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: The architect plans the cores, lobbies, pits and openings and coordinates them. The engineers and the maker size the equipment.

q: A restaurant needs to move trays and small goods between floors, but not people. Which device fits?
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: A dumbwaiter is a small lift for goods only, too small for a person to ride. A service elevator is bigger and more costly.

q: Which system suits continuous travel along a long, level airport corridor?
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Moving walks carry people over long horizontal distances. Escalators and elevators change level.

q: Which pair consists entirely of air-distribution components?
ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
n: Grilles and diffusers are both HVAC air-distribution parts. The other pairs mix elevator and escalator parts.

q: A 40-storey office tower needs fast service to many floors. What is its main vertical transport?
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Elevator banks, often zoned into low-, mid- and high-rise groups, give selective service to many floors. Escalators would be far too slow over 40 storeys.

q: Which pair consists entirely of escalator components?
ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.
n: The comb plate and step chain are both escalator parts: one is the landing transition, the other drives the steps.

q: Why is a horizontal moving walk kept slow, usually about 0.5 m/s?
o: So people can step on and off safely
So the motor can be as small as possible
Because codes require it to match walking speed exactly
So it uses no power when idle
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Riders step from still floor onto the moving surface. Faster walks need special acceleration zones at the ends.

q: Which system suits heavy, continuous pedestrian flow between two adjacent mall levels?
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Escalators move many people between adjacent levels without waiting. One unit can carry thousands of people an hour.

q: Why are elevator shafts and major duct shafts fixed early in schematic design?
o: They can be moved easily later since they are hollow
They affect only the roof plan
They run through every floor, so they fix structure, floor plates and MEP routes
Their size is set by the elevator brand alone
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: Vertical shafts must line up through every level. Moving them later changes beams, slabs and every floor plan.

q: What is the main drawback of escalators for tall buildings?
o: They cannot carry many people at once
They need a tall hoistway and a pit
They can move in one direction only
They serve only one floor to the next, so long trips are slow
ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
n: A rider must change escalators at every floor. For more than a few floors, elevators are faster.
